research_framework.canonical_name: Human Judgment as Structural Constraint in AI-Mediated Complex Systems

framework_description.en: A research framework examining where human judgment, responsibility, confirmation, traceability, and decision boundaries must remain in AI-mediated complex systems.
framework_description.zh: 一项研究人类判断、责任归属、人类确认、可追溯性与决策边界如何在 AI 介导的复杂系统中继续保留的研究框架。

core_models.name: Structural Boundary Framework
core_models.description: Where human judgment becomes structurally necessary.

core_models.name: Responsibility Drift
core_models.description: How accountability becomes fragmented, hidden, or displaced.

core_models.name: Decision Arbitration Framework
core_models.description: How competing directions are brought toward an executable decision.

enterprise_value.primary_focus: Enterprise AI Governance and Decision Architecture

positioning.en: I help organizations clarify human judgment, responsibility, and decision boundaries in AI-assisted systems.
positioning.zh: 我帮助企业厘清 AI 系统中的人类判断、责任归属与决策边界。

problems_addressed: Fragmented responsibility across teams, vendors, platforms, and models
Mixed public information, private assets, and operational systems
Operational risk before AI outputs become real-world action

stable_public_statements.en: AI can move fast. Humans remain responsible for getting it right.
Wherever content travels, its source should remain attached.
stable_public_statements.zh: 内容走到哪，出处跟到哪。

stable_public_statements.en: A human confirmation click does not necessarily mean that a human has taken responsibility.
stable_public_statements.zh: 不是有人点了确认，就代表有人真正负责。

stable_public_statements.en: Service is not a keyword. It means someone receives the request, someone performs the work, and someone remains responsible.
stable_public_statements.zh: 服务不是关键词，服务是有人接、有人做、有人负责。

stable_public_statements.en: Human judgment cannot be removed from systems where uncertainty, consequence, and responsibility remain human.
stable_public_statements.zh: 只要不确定性、后果与责任仍然由人承担，人类判断就不能从系统中被移除。

public_papers.title: Human Judgment as an Irreducible Interface
